title: Pilot-to-production conversion for enterprise agents is reported as very low, but the measurement is unaudited
problem: Every vendor blog quotes a different single-digit production rate for enterprise agents, and I cannot tell whether the number describes my situation.
symptom: Widely repeated statistics with no consistent definition of 'in production', traced back to surveys that are cited but not linked.
why_now: The claim drives real budget decisions while the underlying instruments are not comparable: adoption, pilot, scaled deployment and production are used interchangeably across reports.
existing: Vendor state-of-the-industry reports: useful signal, but self-selected respondents and shifting definitions.
Analyst notes: usually paywalled, so the definition cannot be checked.

evidence.title: AI Agent Reality Check: hype to production gap (agentmarketcap.ai)
evidence.quote: A March 2026 survey found that 78% of enterprises have AI agent pilots - but fewer than 15% have successfully scaled even one agent to organization-wide operational use. Only 11% run agents in production at all.
evidence.note: DELIBERATELY RETAINED AS A BELOW-FLOOR RECORD. The survey itself is not linked, so this is a secondary summary of an unverified instrument. It scores confidence 1 and is excluded from the ranking until a primary source with a stated definition and methodology is attached. This record exists to demonstrate that the credibility ladder is enforced rather than decorative.

build_hypothesis: Before this gap can be ranked, resolve it to the primary survey and record the exact definition of 'in production' used.
